Diagnose and fix the user-reported handling defect on the current BMW M5 driving lab: as soon as the car attempts essentially any high-speed turn, it spins out. Work from the current branch, which already includes the recent tyre-grip, Digital Driver V3, active-differential continuity, and showcase-track jitter fixes. Treat the symptom as a root-cause physics/control problem, not permission to make the car artificially stable. Reproduce or characterize the failure with deterministic 100-180 km/h maneuvers, inspect wheel loads/Fx/Fy/slip angles/slip ratios, yaw rate, sideslip, steering angle, rear-steer angle, drivetrain torque, assist activity, and yaw-moment closure. Check left/right mirrored cases. Do not simply add grip, lower steering globally, add hidden yaw damping/ESC torque, soften suspension, change brake bias, or clamp yaw. Preserve AGENTS.md, PHYSICS_CONVENTIONS.md, and M5_VALIDATION.md as hard constraints. If a defect is found, propose the smallest physically defensible patch with deterministic regression coverage that would fail on the current behavior and pass after the fix. Any patch affecting overall M5 physics must include npm run test:conventions and npm run test:m5-validation:strict in tests_to_run, plus the most relevant high-speed cornering/step-steer/skidpad regression.

XHIGH RUN REQUIREMENT: Use Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor Free through OpenCode Zen Responses API with reasoning effort xhigh. Run all 30 specialist lanes.

XHIGH CONTEXT-RICH RERUN: rerun all 30 specialist lanes with the core-physics-priority context pack and 40k completion budget. Re-evaluate the current high-speed spin diagnosis from scratch; do not rely on prior conclusions.
